concerns.text: The plan compares the filtered model (trained CPU‑only on a 50 M‑parameter diffusion model) against the PhysisForcing baseline, which in the original work uses joint‑optimization and typically GPU‑accelerated training. This introduces a confound: differences in compute resources and training regime may drive performance gaps, not the post‑generation filter alone. The methodology must either (a) replicate the PhysisForcing training conditions (same hardware, joint‑optimization) for a fair comparison, or (b) clearly justify why hardware differences do not affect the equivalence claim.

concerns.location: plan.md:Evaluation – compute R‑Bench and PAI‑Bench scores
concerns.text: R‑Bench and PAI‑Bench are used as proxies for physical‑consistency (construct validity). The plan cites RoboBench 2023 for a correlation > 0.85, but does not provide direct evidence that these benchmarks capture the specific physics dimensions (trajectory continuity, contact conservation) targeted by the filter. Relying solely on proxy scores may weaken construct validity; the methodology should include a direct physics metric (e.g., MuJoCo‑derived continuity/contact scores) as a primary outcome or provide stronger citation support.

concerns.location: plan.md:Statistical testing – run Two‑One‑Sided Tests (TOST) with a 15 % equivalence margin, power ≥ 0.80, α = 0.05, d = 0.5
concerns.text: The power analysis assumes n ≥ 64 per condition, yet the plan generates only 200 videos total (≈ 120 retained after filtering). It is unclear how many evaluation samples will be used for the TOST. The plan mentions generating “at least 64 new robotic manipulation videos” per model, but does not detail how this sample size will be achieved given the retained dataset size and augmentation policy. The methodology must explicitly state the intended evaluation sample size per condition and confirm it meets the power requirement.

concerns.location: plan.md:Augmentation – if curated < 30, augment to reach n ≥ 30
concerns.text: When the curated set is small, physics‑preserving augmentations are applied and the augmented samples are excluded from the primary TOST analysis but are included in model training. This creates a potential bias: the filtered model may benefit from synthetic data that the baseline model does not receive, confounding the effect of the filter itself. The methodology should either (a) keep training data identical across conditions (no augmentation for either), or (b) conduct a sensitivity analysis to quantify the impact of augmentation on the equivalence test.

The plan mentions a Bonferroni‑adjusted α for the TOST but does not clarify the number of hypotheses being corrected for. If only a single equivalence test is performed, Bonferroni adjustment is unnecessary and reduces power. The methodology should justify the correction or remove it to preserve the planned 0.05 family‑wise error rate.
